---
title: "as.Date() on a date-time ignores its time zone"
ref: DAT-01
categories: [Dates]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'as.Date(as.POSIXct("2022-03-04 00:35", tz = "Europe/Paris"))'
reponse: '"2022-03-03"'
attendu: "`\"2022-03-04\"`, the day displayed"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
h <- as.POSIXct("2022-03-04 00:35:51", tz = "Europe/Paris")
h
as.Date(h)
```
:::

## Why

A `POSIXct` is a number of seconds since 1 January 1970 in universal time, along with a time zone that is only used for display. `as.Date()` defaults to `tz = "UTC"` and does not look at that time zone. Yet 00:35 in Paris is still 23:35 the previous day in UTC.

Every time between midnight and 1 a.m. (2 a.m. in summer) therefore lands on the wrong day. On a timestamped dataset, the error only hits a small share of the rows, which makes it hard to spot. {lubridate}, for its part, uses the object's time zone: `as_date(h)` and `as.Date(h)` do not give the same day.

## The remedy

Pass the time zone explicitly.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
as.Date(h, tz = "Europe/Paris")
as.Date(h, tz = attr(h, which = "tzone"))
```
:::
